mainTopic: Why are the כותים forbidden to marry into the Jewish people? The גמרא tries to explain רבי אלעזר's view and ends with רבין's report of three different opinions.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא tried to explain why רבי אלעזר forbids marrying כותים. Its first explanation is a chain: רבי אלעזר follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds that כותים converted only out of fear of lions, and רבי ישמעאל follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that the child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. The גמרא challenges this. רבי ישמעאל needed a פסוק to show that a non-Jew or slave disqualifies a woman, and that would be obvious if their child were a ממזר. So the גמרא says רבי אלעזר himself holds both views. That fails too, because רבי אלעזר said a ממזר comes only from an ערוה punishable by כרת. Finally רבין reports that there are three opinions about the כותים. רבי ישמעאל says they are lion converts and unfit Jews mixed in among them. רבי עקיבא says they are true converts and the כהנים among them were fit. He holds they were forbidden because of how they did יבום with betrothed women, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last link: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the earlier claim that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence that started before this section: רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא. This sets up the explanation that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said רבי אלעזר follows רבי ישמעאל. Now it adds a second link: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי עקיבא. On its own the line is unclear, so the next step spells out what each link means.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like (agrees with the opinion of)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the chain of agreement that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא's position.

steps.title: Explaining the chain: כותים are not real converts, and their children are ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both links. רבי ישמעאל holds that כותים are 'lion converts', so they count as non-Jews. רבי עקיבא holds that the child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר holds like רבי ישמעאל, who said: כותים are 'lion converts.' And רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי עקיבא, who said: if a non-Jew or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what each 'holds like' means. Put together, the two links explain why רבי אלעזר forbids marrying כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Link one: the כותים converted only out of fear of lions, so they are still non-Jews. Link two: a child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. Over time some Jews married כותים, so their descendants may be ממזרים, and that is why marrying them is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The Samaritans, a people settled in ארץ ישראל who converted
'Lion converts': people who converted out of fear, not sincerely
A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew
Child, offspring

steps.whatToRemember: The chain: רבי אלעזר follows רבי ישמעאל (כותים are not real converts), and רבי ישמעאל follows רבי עקיבא (the child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar holds like Rabbi Yishmael,
who said: Samaritans are 'lion converts.'
phrases.notes: See מלכים ב 17:25-26. Lions attacked them, so they converted out of fear and not sincerely.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: נׇכְרִי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: who said: a non-Jew or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman,
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the meaning of each 'holds like' in the chain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific opinions of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא are meant?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל's view that כותים are lion converts, and רבי עקיבא's view that the child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי ישמעאל needed a פסוק to disqualify the woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי ישמעאל really agrees with רבי עקיבא. It quotes רבי יוחנן citing רבי ישמעאל, who brings a פסוק to show that a non-Jew or slave disqualifies a woman from כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי ישמעאל really hold like רבי עקיבא? רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: How do we know that a non-Jew or slave who has relations with a כהן's daughter, a לוי's daughter, or a ישראל's daughter disqualifies her? Because the פסוק says: 'And a כהן's daughter who becomes a widow or divorced, and has no children...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to challenge the second link of the chain. It brings a teaching of רבי ישמעאל that will be used against him in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל looks for a source in the תורה for a rule: a woman who has relations with a non-Jew or a slave becomes disqualified. The fact that he needs a source at all is what the גמרא will build its question on.

keyTerms.meaning: But does...? (opening a challenge)
But didn't (so-and-so) say...?
From where do we know?
They disqualified her

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי סָבַר לָהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yishmael really hold like Rabbi Akiva?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
From where do we know about a non-Jew or a slave
who had relations with a Kohen's daughter or a Levi's daughter
or a Yisrael's daughter, that they disqualified her?
phrases.notes: He means she can no longer marry a כהן, or eat תרומה if she is a כהן's daughter.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And a Kohen's daughter, if she becomes
a widow or divorced, and has no children'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לָהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second link of the chain (רבי ישמעאל following רבי עקיבא).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא that the child of a non-Jew is a ממזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל needs a פסוק to show the woman is disqualified, which suggests he does not treat this union as one that produces a ממזר.

steps.title: How רבי ישמעאל learns it from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of a husband who can leave a woman widowed or divorced, meaning a Jew. This leaves out a non-Jew or slave, who cannot. So a כהן's daughter who was with one of them does not go back to her earlier status.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק speaks of someone who can make her a widow or a divorcee. That leaves out a non-Jew or a slave, who cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting רבי ישמעאל and shows how he reads the פסוק. This is still part of the quoted teaching used in the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's daughter who married a Jew and became a widow or divorced, with no children, may return to eating תרומה. The words 'widow and divorced' point only to a husband a marriage can exist with, a Jew. A non-Jew or slave cannot marry her, so after being with him she stays disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Widowhood
Divorce
Excludes; leaves out

phrases.english: Someone who can bring about widowhood and divorce,
phrases.notes: He means a husband whose marriage to her is real, so it can end by his death or by a divorce. That is a Jewish husband.

phrases.english: excludes a non-Jew or a slave,
who cannot bring about widowhood and divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק quoted in the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jew or slave, who cannot marry a Jewish woman, disqualifies her through relations. This is learned from the words 'widow and divorced'.

steps.title: If the child were a ממזר, why would a פסוק be needed?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי ישמעאל held like רבי עקיבא that the child is a ממזר, it would be obvious that the woman is disqualified. His need for a פסוק shows he does not agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think he holds like רבי עקיבא, then since the child is a ממזר, do we even need a source that she is disqualified by being with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its point. רבי ישמעאל's search for a source shows he cannot agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A union that produces a ממזר is a seriously forbidden union. A woman in such a union is clearly disqualified from כהונה, so no special פסוק would be needed. Since רבי ישמעאל did need one, the union must not produce a ממזר in his view, and this breaks the chain from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you thought)
Now (if this is so)
Is it necessary? (it is obvious)
Relations (between a man and a woman)

steps.whatToRemember: The argument: 'If the child is a ממזר, the disqualification is obvious.' Since רבי ישמעאל needed a פסוק, he apparently does not agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether the woman is disqualified. Everyone agrees she is. The question is only why רבי ישמעאל needed a פסוק if the child is a ממזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the explanation of רבי אלעזר's ban on כותים falls apart, because it depended on רבי ישמעאל agreeing with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And if you would think
that he holds like Rabbi Akiva,
now, if the child is a mamzer,
do we even need to say that he disqualifies her by having relations with her?!
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the non-Jew or slave. If their child is a ממזר, of course she's disqualified, so why would we need a פסוק?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the quoted teaching and turns it into the full challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the child were a ממזר, the woman's disqualification would be obvious. So רבי ישמעאל's need for a פסוק shows he does not consider the child a ממזר.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אלעזר is the one who holds both views
steps.stepSummary: After showing that רבי ישמעאל does not agree with רבי עקיבא, the גמרא suggests that רבי אלעזר is the one who combines the two views.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר holds like רבי ישמעאל, who says that כותים are lion converts. He also holds like רבי עקיבא, who says that when a non-Jew or a slave is with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 5 showed that רבי ישמעאל can't be the one who holds both ideas. So the גמרא moves the same pair of ideas over to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of the explanation stays the same: כותים count as non-Jews, and a non-Jew with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר. Only the person changes, from רבי ישמעאל to רבי אלעזר, who has no פסוק pulling him the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the last answer and offers a new one)
The חכם the גמרא now credits with combining both views

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar holds like Rabbi Yishmael,
who says: Kusim are lion converts.
And he also holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who says: a non-Jew or a slave
who is with a Jewish woman,
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 5 by moving the combined view from רבי ישמעאל to רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the combined view to רבי אלעזר himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל combined his own view with רבי עקיבא's.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר is the one who combines רבי ישמעאל's view on כותים with רבי עקיבא's view on ממזרות.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר said a ממזר comes only from an ערוה with כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer: רבי אלעזר himself said everyone agrees that a ממזר comes only from a forbidden relationship punishable by כרת. A non-Jew's relationship with a Jewish woman doesn't fit that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אלעזר really hold like רבי עקיבא? But רבי אלעזר said: even though בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about צרות, they agree that a ממזר comes only from a relationship that is an ערוה and punishable by כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 6 by quoting a statement from רבי אלעזר himself that seems to go against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says that, according to everyone, a ממזר comes only from an ערוה punishable by כרת. A non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman is not an ערוה with כרת. So רבי אלעזר would say the child is not a ממזר, which is the opposite of רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he really hold this? (opens a challenge)
Rival wives: the other wives of the dead brother in a case of יבום
A forbidden close-relative relationship
Punished with כרת (being cut off)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get caught up in the argument about צרות. It is mentioned only to say: even though בית שמאי and בית הלל argue there, they agree about the rule for a ממזר.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Elazar really hold like Rabbi Akiva?
But Rabbi Elazar said:
Even though they argued,
Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel, about rival wives,
phrases.notes: This is the argument about whether a rival wife of a woman forbidden to the brother-in-law must do יבום.

phrases.english: they agree that a mamzer comes only
from someone whose prohibition is a forbidden-relative prohibition
and is punished with kares!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 6 using רבי אלעזר's own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי עקיבא that the child of a non-Jew and a Jewish woman is a ממזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר limits ממזר to the child of an ערוה with כרת. A non-Jew with a Jewish woman is not such a case, so he cannot agree with רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבין reports three opinions about the כותים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier approach and brings רבין's report, passed down through one of three possible chains, that there are three opinions on this matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן. Some say it was רבי אבא בר זבדא quoting רבי חנינא, and some say it was רבי יעקב בר אידי quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי. They said: there are three opinions on this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: Both earlier attempts failed, so the גמרא starts fresh with a report that there are three separate opinions about the כותים. This line sets up the next steps, which lay out each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of having one תנא combine two views, the גמרא now says different תנאים had different reasons for treating כותים as forbidden. The long chain of names is only a doubt about who passed the report down; it does not change what the report says.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל with a teaching)
And some say (another version of who said it)
Three opinions (three ways of seeing the matter)
On this matter (the status of the כותים)

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said
that Rabbi Chanina said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לָהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
There are three opinions on this matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 7 knocks out the רבי אלעזר answer, this opens a brand-new approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Starting over with a new framework of three separate opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One תנא held both רבי ישמעאל's and רבי עקיבא's views together.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are three separate opinions about the כותים, each with its own reason.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: unfit כהנים mixed in among the lion converts
steps.stepSummary: The first of the three opinions: רבי ישמעאל holds that כותים are lion converts, and unfit כהנים from the Jewish people had mixed in with them. That is why they were disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל holds: כותים are lion converts, and the כהנים who mixed in among them were unfit כהנים. As it says, 'And they made for themselves, from among themselves, priests of the high places.' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this means from the 'thorns' among the people. Because of this, they were disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the first of the three opinions, רבי ישמעאל's. The problem with the כותים comes from flawed Jews who mixed in among them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל doesn't need רבי עקיבא's rule about ממזרים at all. The כותים themselves are non-Jews, but Jews with a flawed status, like unfit כהנים, became mixed in among them. Since any כותי might be one of these flawed Jews, they were all disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed in and blended among them
Unfit כהנים (with a flawed family status)
From among themselves (here read as related to קוֹצִים, thorns)
Thorns: here, people with a flawed status
They disqualified them

steps.confusionAlert: According to רבי ישמעאל, the problem is not that the כותים are non-Jews. It is the flawed Jews who blended in among them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the need to pair רבי ישמעאל with רבי עקיבא, which is what broke down in steps 3–5. It gives רבי ישמעאל his own reason for forbidding the כותים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds:
Kusim are lion converts,
and the kohanim who mixed in among them
were unfit kohanim,
as it says: "And they made for themselves
from among themselves priests of the high places,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and Rabbah bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
From the thorns among the people.
phrases.notes: He reads מִקְצוֹתָם as if it came from קוֹצִים, thorns, meaning the people with a flawed status.

phrases.english: And because of this they disqualified them.
phrases.notes: The reason is these flawed Jews mixed in among the כותים, not the כותים themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: כּוּתִים גֵּירֵי אֲרָיוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the three opinions announced in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, כותים are lion converts, but unfit כהנים from the Jewish people mixed in among them (based on מקצותם, from the thorns among the people). That is why the כותים were disqualified.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's View: The כותים Were True Converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that כותים are גירי אמת and that the כהנים who blended in with them were fit כהנים. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: כותים are true converts, and the כהנים who blended in among them were fit כהנים. As it says: 'And they made for themselves, from among themselves, priests of the high places.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second of the three opinions in רבין's report. רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל on both points: the conversion and the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said the כותים converted only out of fear of the lions, and that unfit כהנים mixed in with them. רבי עקיבא says the opposite on both counts: their conversion was real, and the כהנים among them were kosher. The פסוק about 'priests of the high places' is his source that real כהנים joined them.

keyTerms.meaning: The people settled in the land of Israel by the king of Assyria, who later converted
True converts who converted sincerely
Blended in, assimilated
Priests who served at the private altars (high places)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
Samaritans are true converts,
and the priests who blended in among them
were fit priests,
as it is stated: 'And they made for themselves, from among themselves, priests of the high places,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the second of the three opinions in רבין's report, opposite to רבי ישמעאל's view in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים are גירי אמת, and the כהנים who blended in with them were כשרים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Explains the Verse: From the Chosen Ones
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן, who explains that 'from among themselves' in the פסוק means 'from the chosen ones of the people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'From among themselves' means from the chosen ones of the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves רבי עקיבא's point. רבי יוחנן reads the key word as 'the best of the people.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, the פסוק only says the כותים appointed priests. רבי יוחנן reads מקצותם as 'from the chosen ones,' so these were real, well-born כהנים from the Jewish people. That supports רבי עקיבא's claim that the כהנים among the כותים were fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'from their ends.' Here it is read as 'from their choicest'
The chosen, finest members of the people

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
From the chosen ones of the people.
phrases.notes: He is explaining the word מקצותם from the פסוק: these priests came from the best families.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 10 supports רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's claim that the כהנים among the כותים were fit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's reading of מקצותם in מלכים ב 17:32 as 'from the chosen ones of the people.'

steps.title: If Their Lineage Was Fine, Why Were They Forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי עקיבא, there is no problem with the conversion or with the כהנים, so why did the חכמים forbid the כותים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for what reason did they forbid them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that comes straight out of רבי עקיבא's view. It is setting up the next step, which gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the reason was clear: the flawed Jews, like unfit כהנים, who mixed in among the כותים. רבי עקיבא holds that the conversion was real and the כהנים were fit, so we still need to know why the כותים were forbidden from marrying into the community.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason?
They forbade them (from marrying into the Jewish community)

phrases.english: And if so, for what reason did they forbid them?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים, who forbade marrying כותים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from רבי עקיבא's view once both lineage problems are removed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כותים were forbidden, according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Because They Did יבום With Betrothed Women
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כותים were forbidden because they performed יבום with women who were only betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they would perform יבום with betrothed women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. The problem was not their lineage but their wrong practice of יבום, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem shifts from where the כותים came from to how they behaved. Their way of doing יבום with an ארוסה did not follow הלכה, and that is what led to the prohibition. The גמרא goes on to explain exactly what was wrong with this practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Performing יבום (levirate marriage)
Women who are betrothed (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A brother marrying the widow of his brother who died childless

steps.confusionAlert: Doing יבום with an ארוסה is not wrong in itself. The problem lies in how the כותים handled it, which the גמרא explains at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: Because they would perform levirate marriage with betrothed women

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כותים were forbidden because of their improper practice of יבום with betrothed women, not because of their lineage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that for רבי עקיבא, the prohibition on כותים comes from how they behaved, not from flawed ancestry.
